briefs.headline: Russell 2000 rises 0.7% as smaller companies beat tech giants again
briefs.summary: The Russell 2000 is up 4.7% this week and 9% for 2026, beating the S&P 500's 4.9% and the Nasdaq's 1.5% this year. Smaller stocks like Joby Aviation (up 11.6%), AMC (up 8.8%) and GoPro (up 7.0%) were among the biggest gainers on Wednesday. On November 18 Russell 2000 futures had hit their lowest level since April 13, so the index has bounced back fast. Shoppers' spending rose 0.3% in October and incomes rose 0.7%.
bull: Small companies beat the big indexes again on Nov 25, rising 0.71% while the Nasdaq fell 0.62%, as money moved away from AI giants.

briefs.headline: Micron slips 4.5% more as BNP Paribas cuts its target to $775 from $1,700
briefs.about: Micron makes memory chips, the parts that store data in computers, phones and the giant data centers that run AI. Its main products are DRAM and NAND flash memory, plus HBM, a fast memory built for AI chips.
briefs.summary: BNP Paribas lowered Micron to Neutral (no strong view either way) and expects memory supply and demand to balance by mid-2027. Research firm SemiAnalysis cut its forecasts for AI chip spending on November 13 by 19% for 2027 and 28% for 2028. Huawei plans to show its own HBM memory design at a chip conference in February, and US rules already stop Micron from selling HBM to China. Micron has about $150 billion of signed orders it has not yet delivered, Blockonomi reported.
bull: Micron's $150 billion of signed but undelivered orders, from 26 long-term customer agreements, locks in a lot of future sales even if prices soften.
Even after the drop, 28 of 30 analysts tracked by TipRanks rate it a Buy, with an average target of $1,574, and Citi keeps a $1,300 target.
Micron brought in $43.97 billion of cash from its business last quarter, giving it a big cushion if the memory market cools.
bear: BNP Paribas cut its target 54%, from $1,700 to $775, a sign that even some fans now think memory prices have peaked.
TrendForce expects NAND supply to grow 25% to 30% next year; more supply than demand usually pushes memory prices down.
SemiAnalysis cut its 2030 AI chip spending forecast by 40%, and Micron's biggest growth has come from memory for AI chips.

briefs.name: Micron Technology
briefs.whyMoved: Micron had a wild Thanksgiving week: it closed at $594.51 on Friday, November 20, jumped 19% to $707.70 on Monday, fell 11% to $629.79 on Tuesday, and dropped another 4.53% on Wednesday, November 25, to about $601. It has lost nearly half its value since June. The worries are about memory prices: TrendForce said on November 19 that NAND flash prices could stay flat or fall in early 2027, and it expects world NAND supply to grow 25% to 30% next year while Chinese cloud companies trimmed their 2027 orders. That matters because Micron kept 87 cents of every sales dollar as gross profit last quarter, which only happens when memory is scarce, so more supply and lower prices would shrink profit fast.

watch.what: US Senate hearing tied to Nvidia. Calm news could help chip stocks; new problems for Nvidia could pull Micron lower again.
Fed rate decision. A hike is widely expected; signs of more hikes would hurt fast-moving chip stocks like Micron.

briefs.headline: Domino's gets an upgrade to a $400 target, but US store sales grew just 0.3%
briefs.about: Domino's Pizza is the world's biggest pizza delivery chain. Most of its stores are run by franchise owners, who pay Domino's fees and buy dough, cheese and other supplies from it.
briefs.whyMoved: Domino's rose about 2.5% on the morning of November 13 after the research firm Baird upgraded it to 'outperform' and raised its target to $400 from $320, about 20% above the prior day's close. Baird sees a 'clearer path' to better sales because the average order size grew in the third quarter and Domino's is shortening its discount deals and adding menu items people add on. The rest of the two weeks was quiet, and the stock is still down more than 18% in 2026. Domino's makes most of its money from fees franchise owners pay on their sales and from selling them supplies, so its profit depends on sales at existing stores, which grew only 0.3% in the US last quarter.
briefs.summary: Third-quarter revenue was $1.19 billion and profit was $4.60 a share, both above what analysts expected. Global retail sales rose 3.2% to $4.84 billion, slower than 6.3% a year earlier, and international same-store sales rose just 0.2%. On October 30 Domino's lowered its 2026 goal for new US stores and for operating profit growth, citing pressure on franchise owners' profits. BMO Capital also rates Domino's 'outperform' with a $390 target, while 16 of 30 analysts say hold.
bull: Baird's November 13 upgrade to a $400 target points to bigger average orders, which matter because more money per order helps both Domino's and its franchise owners.
Profit per share rose to $4.60 from $4.08 a year earlier, even though US store sales barely grew.
13 of 30 analysts rate Domino's a buy and only 1 says sell, with targets as high as $425.
bear: US same-store sales grew only 0.3% last quarter, down from 5.2% a year earlier, and the CFO expects 2026 growth at the low end of low single digits.
Domino's cut its 2026 goal for new US stores on October 30, and Baird warns weaker 2026 results will likely slow store openings in 2027 too.
Markets expect a Fed rate hike at the December 8-9 meeting, and higher rates make it costlier for franchise owners to borrow money to open stores.

watch.what: Fed rate decision. A hike is expected; more hikes would raise franchise owners' borrowing costs and could slow new store openings.
